channel.title: How Biscuit
channel.description: Practical, evidence-aware guides for technology, home, kitchens, shopping decisions, and useful tools.

item.title: Can You Freeze Milk?
item.description: You can freeze pasteurized milk in a freezer-safe container with expansion space, then thaw it in the refrigerator. Texture may separate, so shake or blend it after thawing.

item.title: Can You Mix Bleach and Vinegar?
item.description: Never mix chlorine bleach and vinegar. The combination can release toxic chlorine gas. Leave the area for fresh air and contact emergency or poison help if exposure occurs.

item.title: Can You Plug an Air Conditioner Into an Extension Cord?
item.description: A room air conditioner should normally plug directly into a grounded wall outlet, not an extension cord. Here is the safe response when its factory cord will not reach.

item.title: Do You Have to Preheat the Oven?
item.description: Preheat for most baking and whenever a recipe or package says to. Some roasts and casseroles can start in a cold oven, but food-safety temperatures still govern doneness.

item.title: How Long Does Cooked Rice Last in the Fridge?
item.description: Refrigerate cooked rice within two hours and use it within four days. Cool it promptly in shallow containers and reheat leftovers to 165°F.

item.title: How Often Should You Test and Replace Smoke Alarms?
item.description: Test smoke alarms at least monthly and replace the whole alarm when it is 10 years old, or sooner if its instructions or failed tests require it.

item.title: What Temperature Should a Refrigerator Be?
item.description: Keep the refrigerator at 40°F or below and the freezer at 0°F. Verify the actual temperature with an appliance thermometer and allow air to circulate.

item.title: Why Does My Dishwasher Leave a White Film on Dishes?
item.description: White film on dishwasher loads is often mineral residue or detergent film, but permanent glass etching can look similar. Use a simple wipe test, then adjust water, detergent, and rinse aid.

item.title: Why Does My GFCI Outlet Keep Tripping?
item.description: A GFCI that keeps tripping may be detecting leakage current, moisture, a faulty appliance, or a wiring problem. Use this safe isolation sequence before calling an electrician.

item.title: Why Is My Washing Machine Shaking or Walking?
item.description: A washer often shakes because the load is unbalanced, the machine is not level, or shipping hardware remains installed. Stop it and check in a safe order.

item.title: Can You Plug a Space Heater Into a Power Strip?
item.description: Space heaters should be plugged directly into a wall outlet, not into a power strip or extension cord. Here is why and what to do when the cord will not reach.

item.title: Can You Put Hot Food Directly in the Refrigerator?
item.description: Hot food can go directly into the refrigerator, but large batches should be divided into shallow containers so they cool quickly and safely.

item.title: Can You Use Soap on Cast Iron?
item.description: Yes. A small amount of mild dish soap is generally safe for seasoned cast iron. Wash by hand, dry promptly, and apply a very thin coat of oil if needed.

item.title: Does a Dishwasher Use Less Water Than Hand-Washing?
item.description: A modern dishwasher, especially an ENERGY STAR certified model run with full loads, usually uses less water than washing the same dishes by hand under a running faucet.

item.title: How Long Can Cooked Food Sit Out?
item.description: Most perishable cooked food should be refrigerated within two hours, or within one hour when the temperature is above 90°F. Food held safely hot or cold follows different rules.

item.title: How to Clean a Dishwasher Filter
item.description: A removable dishwasher filter can collect food, grit, labels, and debris. Here is how to locate, clean, inspect, and reinstall it without damaging the machine.

item.title: Power Strip vs. Surge Protector: What Is the Difference?
item.description: Power strips add outlets. Surge protectors also contain components intended to limit certain voltage surges. Here is how to tell what you own and what neither device can safely do.

item.title: Should You Rinse Dishes Before Putting Them in the Dishwasher?
item.description: Usually, no. Scrape off solid food and load the dishwasher without hand-rinsing. Modern machines and detergents are designed to do the washing.

item.title: Why Do LED Light Bulbs Flicker?
item.description: LED flicker commonly comes from an incompatible dimmer, a non-dimmable bulb, a poor driver, a loose connection, or unstable power. Here is how to narrow it down safely.

item.title: Why Do Windows Condense in Winter?
item.description: Winter window condensation forms when humid indoor air meets glass cold enough to fall below the air’s dew point. Here is how to reduce it and when it signals a larger moisture problem.

item.title: Do Ceiling Fans Cool a Room? What They Actually Do
item.description: Ceiling fans make people feel cooler by moving air, but they do not meaningfully lower an empty room’s temperature. Here is when to run one, when to turn it off, and how to pair it with air conditioning.

item.title: Air-Drying vs. Clothes Dryer: Cost, Time, and Fabric Tradeoffs
item.description: Air drying reduces dryer energy and can reduce fabric wear, but requires time, space, ventilation, and humidity control. Compare cost, weather, pollen, and fabric needs.

item.title: Air Purifier vs. HVAC Filter: Which Do You Need?
item.description: Portable air cleaners treat one room or area. HVAC filters work throughout a ducted system only while its fan runs. Learn when one, both, or neither solves the problem.

item.title: Appliance Buying Checklist: Measurements, Hookups, Delivery, Warranty, and Recalls
item.description: Measure the space and delivery route, verify every hookup, read EnergyGuide and warranty terms, inspect delivery damage, check recalls, and document installation.

item.title: Are Extended Warranties on Appliances Worth It?
item.description: Compare the service contract with the manufacturer warranty, repair risk, deductibles, exclusions, shipping, reimbursement limits, claims process, and provider reputation.

item.title: Why Are Clothes Taking So Long to Dry?
item.description: Long drying time often starts with airflow, lint, venting, load size, washer spin, sensors, cycle choice, room temperature, or a heating fault. Check safety before running another cycle.

item.title: Cold vs. Warm vs. Hot Water for Laundry
item.description: Cold water saves the most energy and works for many ordinary loads. Warm or hot water may be needed for oily soil, care-label instructions, sanitation, or exact detergent and washer requirements.

item.title: ENERGY STAR vs. EnergyGuide
item.description: EnergyGuide reports standardized energy use and comparison information. ENERGY STAR is a voluntary efficiency certification for eligible products meeting current criteria.

item.title: Why Does My Front-Load Washer Smell?
item.description: Musty odor often comes from moisture and detergent residue in the gasket, dispenser, drum, filter, or drain area. Clean the exact model correctly and prevent moisture from remaining.

item.title: Heat Pump vs. Standard Electric Water Heater
item.description: Heat-pump water heaters move heat from surrounding air and may use resistance backup. Compare efficiency, recovery, room size, temperature, noise, condensate, and installation.

item.title: How Long Do Leftovers Last in the Fridge?
item.description: Most cooked leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in a refrigerator at 40°F or below. Refrigerate within 2 hours, use shallow containers, and reheat leftovers to 165°F.

item.title: How Much Does an Air Purifier Cost to Run?
item.description: Calculate air-purifier electricity from watts, runtime, and your local rate, then add replacement-filter cost. Compare CADR, noise, and energy efficiency rather than watts alone.

item.title: How Much Does a Water Heater Cost to Run?
item.description: Use the EnergyGuide annual kWh, therms, or fuel consumption with your local rate. Water-heater cost depends on type, household demand, setpoint, standby loss, and installation.

item.title: How Much Laundry Detergent Should You Use?
item.description: Use the detergent label for the exact concentration, washer type, load size, soil, and water hardness. More detergent can leave residue, odor, and poor rinsing.

item.title: How Often Should You Change Your HVAC Filter?
item.description: There is no universal 30-, 60-, or 90-day rule. Inspect based on filter depth, system runtime, pets, smoke, renovation dust, airflow, and manufacturer guidance.

item.title: How Often Should You Clean a Dryer Vent?
item.description: Clean the lint filter every load and clean lint from the vent pipe at least annually. Inspect sooner when drying time, airflow, heat, or lint buildup changes.

item.title: How to Read an EnergyGuide Label
item.description: Learn what the yellow EnergyGuide label says about annual energy use, estimated operating cost, similar-model comparisons, capacity, and local-rate recalculation.

item.title: New vs. Used vs. Refurbished vs. Open-Box Appliances
item.description: Condition labels are not standardized. Verify the seller, exact model, serial, recall status, warranty, return policy, missing parts, damage, sanitation, and installation.

item.title: How to Organize a Refrigerator for Food Safety and Less Waste
item.description: Keep the refrigerator at 40°F or below, preserve airflow, contain raw-food leaks, date leftovers, and create a visible use-first area to reduce waste.

item.title: Refrigerator Not Cooling but Freezer Works
item.description: Protect food first, then check blocked vents, overpacking, frost, the evaporator fan, damper, door seals, controls, and model-specific faults.

item.title: Why Is My Refrigerator Running All the Time?
item.description: A refrigerator may run longer because of heat, door openings, a recent grocery load, a low temperature setting, blocked vents, bad seals, dirty coils, or a mechanical fault.

item.title: Repair or Replace an Appliance?
item.description: Safety and recall status come first. Then compare diagnosis confidence, repair cost, repeat failures, support, parts, operating cost, installation, downtime, and replacement cost.

item.title: Should You Unplug Electronics During a Thunderstorm?
item.description: Unplug sensitive electronics before thunder begins, not during an active storm. Learn what to disconnect, what to leave alone, and what surge protectors can actually do.

item.title: Tank vs. Tankless Water Heater: Which Is Better for Your Home?
item.description: Storage heaters provide a hot-water reserve. Tankless units heat on demand but remain limited by flow, temperature rise, gas or electrical service, venting, and simultaneous fixtures.

item.title: Is My Water Heater Leaking? What to Check and When to Shut It Down
item.description: Identify visible leaks at connections, drain valves, relief piping, condensate, drain pans, or the tank body. Shut down safely and call qualified service for active or unsafe leaks.

item.title: What Temperature Should a Water Heater Be Set To?
item.description: For most residential applications, 120°F is the ordinary starting point. Learn how scald risk, bacteria, mixing valves, appliance needs, and system type affect the setting.

item.title: What Can an Air Purifier Remove?
item.description: Air purifiers can reduce some airborne particles such as smoke, dust, pollen, and pet allergens. They do not repair mold, remove radon, or replace carbon-monoxide alarms.

item.title: What MERV Rating Should You Use in Your House?
item.description: EPA recommends MERV 13, or the highest filter your HVAC fan and filter slot can accommodate. Learn how fit, airflow, smoke, pets, and system limits change the answer.

item.title: What Size Air Purifier Do You Need?
item.description: Size an air purifier by room area, ceiling height, target particle, and Clean Air Delivery Rate. EPA's estimate starts around 65 cfm per 100 square feet at an 8-foot ceiling.

item.title: Why Is My Freezer Frosting Up?
item.description: Excess frost usually means moist air is entering or the freezer is not defrosting correctly. Check the door, gasket, alignment, food, vents, drain, and model-specific defrost system.
